fact: IXPN, established 2006, is a neutral exchange where ISPs, operators, content providers and data centres exchange traffic locally; TechTV Network reports IXPN says it is trusted by more than 130 networks, with several points of presence in Lagos data centres.

IXPN has regional connectivity in Abuja and Enugu as well as multiple points of presence in Lagos, per TechTV Network; Digital Realty announced a new IXPN point of presence at its Ibeju-Lekki data centre in April 2026 (Lagos).
Traffic: 1 Tbps (peak) at IXPN on 2025-04-24, a record peak announced by IXPN and reported by TechAfrica News; the article gives no earlier date for the peak.
IXPN is operating, with a participant list of ISPs, banks, fintechs and enterprises, per IT Pulse Nigeria quoting IXPN CEO Muhammed Rudman; the article does not state a member count.
Traffic: 4 Gbps (aggregate peak) at IXPN in 2015, per IT Pulse Nigeria.
Traffic: 1.7 Tbps (aggregate peak) at IXPN in 2025, per IT Pulse Nigeria.
IXPN aggregate peak traffic grew from 4 Gbps in 2015 to 1.7 Tbps in 2025, a 42,400% increase over ten years, per IT Pulse Nigeria.
Global content networks Google, Meta, Microsoft and TikTok are among the current participants (members) at IXPN, per IT Pulse Nigeria; the article gives no date, so its publication date is used.

IXPN is hosted at the MDXi Lekki data centre in Lagos, with direct peering available through MainOne to Amsterdam, Ghana and London exchanges, per Submarine Networks; no date for the statement, so the page date is used.
Rack Centre, the Lagos data centre, states it offers public peering with the Internet Exchange Point of Nigeria (IXPN); date taken from the sheet's published date, 2024-05.
Digital Realty says Medallion's Lagos data centre carries over 80% of the public peering traffic on the Nigerian Internet Exchange, with over 70 carriers and ISPs present.

Tech.Africa says Medallion's Victoria Island data centre in Lagos is the busiest node for the Internet Exchange Point of Nigeria, hosting about 90 networks including IXPN itself; date is the article's, none given for the statement.
TechnoMag says Starlink's Lagos gateway at Equinix's Lekki data centre peers at IXPN Lagos, described as its largest African connection at 600 Gbps (Starlink's connection, not exchange traffic).

CIO Africa says the Internet Exchange Point of Nigeria (IXPN) connects more than 130 members, including telecom operators, internet service providers and global content platforms, and keeps domestic traffic in Nigeria.
CIO Africa says IXPN's more than 130 members include global content platforms, none named.
CIO Africa says IXPN's peak domestic traffic exceeded one terabit per second for the first time in April 2025 and had more than doubled to over two terabits per second by March 2026.
CIO Africa says IXPN, besides its three Lagos points of presence, operates points of presence in Abuja, Port Harcourt, Enugu, Kano, Delta and Gombe.
ITEdgeNews says Akamai connected to the Internet Exchange Point of Nigeria (IXPN) and now peers locally there alongside Google and Facebook.
The Guardian reports IXPN, marking 20 years since 2006, now has over 130 connected networks and over 200 connected ports.
The Guardian reports IXPN has 13 points of presence nationwide.

BusinessDay reports the Internet Exchange Point of Nigeria (IXPN), established in 2006, lets ISPs, operators and content delivery networks exchange traffic locally, with peering centred on Digital Realty's Medallion data centre.
WACREN says it established the Lagos GXP, linked by 10 Gbps to ZAOXI in Cape Town and connecting to Internet2, CANARIE, RedCLARA, CSTNET, ANSP and GEANT.
WACREN says the Lagos GXP connects to research networks abroad and interconnects with ZAOXI in South Africa.
